title: Baguio cracks down on vendors selling spoiled food
summary: BAGUIO CITY, Philippines — Mayor Benjamin Magalong warned vendors that establishments caught selling spoiled, contaminated, or unfit-for-consumption food would face immediate closure, saying…

blocks.text: BAGUIO CITY, Philippines — Mayor Benjamin Magalong warned vendors that establishments caught selling spoiled, contaminated, or unfit-for-consumption food would face immediate closure, saying violators would not be given a second chance. In a statement on Tuesday, Nov. 17, Magalong said the city government would continue its inspections and enforcement campaign following the recent seizure of spoiled fish at a local establishment. He specifically warned vendors against selling double-dead meat and spoiled agricultural products, saying he would not give violators another chance or entertain appeals once their violations are established.
